items.claim: When a blind SQL injection returns no data, the proof is made of timing: concatenate a deliberately slow operation into the SQL query and look for a repeatable jump in page-load time that the unmodified request does not show.
items.body:
When a blind SQL injection returns no data, the proof is made of timing: concatenate a deliberately slow operation into the SQL query and look for a repeatable jump in page-load time that the unmodified request does not show.

HackTricks reference: SQL Injection (pentesting-web/sql-injection/README.md)
items.disproof: A concatenated slow operation that leaves page-load time flat, or a delay that appears just as often on a control request carrying no injected syntax, refutes it as a blind SQL injection oracle.

items.claim: Once a UNION SELECT column count is aligned, the tester can read a chosen position out of a table with a wildcard select and never has to know the column's name, which is how data leaves the database once the injection point is confirmed.

items.claim: MS Access hands the tester a file-existence oracle from inside the injection: point the database reference at a local file and the invalid-database-format error appears only when that file is really there, so file enumeration is driven by comparing errors across candidate paths.
items.body:

HackTricks reference: MS Access SQL Injection (pentesting-web/sql-injection/ms-access-sql-injection.md)
items.disproof: The invalid-format error appearing identically for names that do not exist, or never appearing for one that does, refutes the existence oracle.

items.claim: Inside an injected MS Access query, TOP and LAST act as row selectors, so the tester can cap or reverse the result set and page out a table's records instead of dumping it whole.

items.disproof: TOP or LAST modifiers rejected as syntax by the same injection point, or accepted but leaving the returned rows unchanged, refute their use as row-selection controls.

items.claim: On MSSQL a single injected UNION SELECT over information_schema.columns hands back the schema, table and column names of the current database at once, and on error-based vectors every selected expression has to carry an alias or the query will not come back.
items.body:
On MSSQL a single injected UNION SELECT over information_schema.columns hands back the schema, table and column names of the current database at once, and on error-based vectors every selected expression has to carry an alias or the query will not come back.

HackTricks reference: MSSQL Injection (pentesting-web/sql-injection/mssql-injection.md)
items.disproof: An error-based injected select that errors purely because an expression lacks an alias, or a schema enumeration that returns no rows despite a working injection point, refutes these requirements.

sources.quote:
Here's how to retrieve the schema, tables, and columns from the current database:

sql
https://vuln.app/getItem?id=-1'+union+select+null,concat_ws(0x3a,table_schema,table_name,column_name),null+from+information_schema.columns+for+json+auto--
In situations where error-based vectors are used, it's crucial to provide an alias or a name.
Weak implementations often look for common SQL injection keywords within the request, so you may be able to bypass these filters by encoding or escaping characters

items.claim: An MSSQL injection point doubles as a privilege-reach probe: calling fn_my_permissions against the database and filtering on a named permission tells the tester which database-level grants the injected session actually holds before they plan any escalation.
items.body:
An MSSQL injection point doubles as a privilege-reach probe: calling fn_my_permissions against the database and filtering on a named permission tells the tester which database-level grants the injected session actually holds before they plan any escalation.

HackTricks reference: MSSQL Injection (pentesting-web/sql-injection/mssql-injection.md)
items.disproof: fn_my_permissions returning no rows, or an empty grant set, for a login that demonstrably holds the named database permission refutes it as a reach check.

sources.quote: SELECT * FROM fn_my_permissions(NULL, 'DATABASE') WHERE permission_name='VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE';

items.claim: On MSSQL the tester can read the live query text back through sys.dm_exec_requests joined to sys.dm_exec_sql_text, which is the way to confirm the injection really landed in the query and to see the surrounding SQL, with the server-level permission checked separately.
items.body:

HackTricks reference: MSSQL Injection (pentesting-web/sql-injection/mssql-injection.md)
items.disproof: The DMVs returning nothing, or returning a query that does not contain the injected syntax, refutes their use for reading back the currently executing SQL query.

sources.quote:
The currently executing SQL query can be retrieved by accessing sys.dm_exec_requests and sys.dm_exec_sql_text:

sql
https://vuln.app/getItem?id=-1%20union%20select%20null,(select+text+from+sys.dm_exec_requests+cross+apply+sys.dm_exec_sql_text(sql_handle)),null,null


To check if you have the VIEW SERVER STATE permission, the following query can be used:

sql
SELECT * FROM fn_my_permissions(NULL, 'SERVER') WHERE permission_name='VIEW SERVER STATE';

items.claim: MySQL schema and table names come out of a UNION SELECT with GROUP_CONCAT over information_schema, and the alternating letter case of the quoted keywords is the point: the enumeration has to be sent in mixed case so a filter matching keywords in one fixed case does not stop it.
items.body:
MySQL schema and table names come out of a UNION SELECT with GROUP_CONCAT over information_schema, and the alternating letter case of the quoted keywords is the point: the enumeration has to be sent in mixed case so a filter matching keywords in one fixed case does not stop it.

HackTricks reference: MySQL injection (pentesting-web/sql-injection/mysql-injection/README.md)
items.disproof: A filter that blocks the mixed-case spelling while letting the all-lowercase form through, or a UNION SELECT that returns no schema rows despite a working injection point, refutes this enumeration route.

items.claim: A search box wired into a full-text MATCH ... AGAINST clause in boolean mode is its own injection flavour: the search term is concatenated inside the quoted argument, so the tester should probe the quote and the boolean-mode operators rather than a plain WHERE value.
items.body:
A search box wired into a full-text MATCH ... AGAINST clause in boolean mode is its own injection flavour: the search term is concatenated inside the quoted argument, so the tester should probe the quote and the boolean-mode operators rather than a plain WHERE value.

HackTricks reference: MySQL injection (pentesting-web/sql-injection/mysql-injection/README.md)
items.disproof: A search parameter concatenated into that MATCH clause that can neither break out of the quotes nor change the boolean-mode search, refutes it as an injection point.
